help.start:
Quick start

Edit subtitles in sync with a video, entirely on your computer. Your original files are never modified.

1

Open your files

Drop a video and an .srt onto the window, or use Open video and Open SRT. Audio files (mp3, wav, m4a) work too.

2

Edit and sync

Click a subtitle to jump to it, type to edit, and fix timing with Sync…, Live timing or by dragging blocks on the timeline.

3

Export

Check the Review tab, then use Export ▾ to save the final SRT or WebVTT wherever you like.

No subtitles yet? Click Transcribe to generate them from the audio with Whisper.
help.edit:
Editing text

EnterSplit the block at the cursor. Time is divided by text length and, with a waveform, moved to the nearest pause.
Alt EnterLine break inside the same block (Shift Enter also works).
Del at the endMerge with the next block (on a Mac keyboard: fn delete).
⌫ at the startMerge with the previous block.
Alt BBalance lines: re-wrap into two lines of similar length without leaving short words dangling.
Alt TShow the subtitle at the top of the screen (exported as {\an8}).
Cmd/Ctrl FFind and replace, with match case and whole word options.

Selecting several subtitles

Shift-click selects a range and Cmd/Ctrl-click adds or removes one. A bar appears to shift, merge, balance or delete them all at once.

Supported formatting: <i>, <b> and <u> tags are shown in the preview and kept on export.
help.sync:
Timing & sync

Two-point sync best for out-of-sync files

  1. Click Sync…. Select a subtitle near the beginning, play until you hear that line, and press Point A (Alt 1).
  2. Do the same with a subtitle near the end: Point B (Alt 2).
  3. Click Apply to all. The offset and the speed are fixed together, and an FPS mismatch is detected for you.

Live timing

Click ● Live timing (Alt M) and hold Space while each line is spoken: press sets the start, release sets the end, and it moves on to the next subtitle. Use ↓ to skip, ↑ to go back and Esc to exit. Lower the playback speed for tricky passages.

Other tools

  • Alt I / Alt O set the start / end of the selected subtitle to the current time.
  • Shift moves all subtitles (or those from the selected one) by a number of seconds.
  • FPS convert rescales times when the subtitle was made for a different frame rate.
  • Ripple following: when you set a start or drag a block, everything after it moves too.

With Snap on, edges stick to the playhead, to neighbouring subtitles (keeping the minimum gap) and to shot changes.

help.quality:
Quality checks

Every subtitle is checked while you type. Problems show in the list, on the timeline and over the video. The limits below are your current settings (change them in ⚙ Settings).

Reading speedAmber above characters per second, red 25% above that.
Line lengthAt most characters per line and lines.
DurationBetween s and s on screen.
GapsNo overlaps, and at least frames between subtitles.
Shot changesStarts and ends within frames of a cut should snap to it.

The Review tab lists every problem with filters. Most have a one-click fix, and Auto-fix handles them all at once. Everything can be undone.
help.translate:
Translation

Click Translation to show the original and the translation side by side with the same timing. Open translation imports a translated SRT and matches it by overlapping times.

In translation mode the quality checks apply to the translation, Enter in the translation column is a line break, and the preview menu (Aa) chooses what is shown over the video. Export each version from Export ▾.
help.transcribe:
Transcription

Transcribe creates subtitles from the audio using Whisper, running inside the app. The audio never leaves your computer; only the model is downloaded the first time.

tiny~40 MB · fastest, good for clear speech.
base~80 MB · a good balance (recommended).
small~250 MB · most accurate, slow without a GPU.

With WebGPU (Chrome, Edge, the desktop app) a minute of audio takes seconds. Results are split and balanced to follow your quality settings. Check the Review tab afterwards.
help.cuts:
Shot changes

Detect cuts scans the video at 16× speed (about 4 minutes per hour of video) and refines to the exact frame the cuts close to a subtitle edge. Keep the window visible while it runs. Cuts appear as purple lines on the timeline and feed the snapping and the quality checks. Detection is approximate, so trust your eyes.
help.save:
Saving & export

  • Every change is saved automatically to a working copy. The original file is never touched.
  • Working copies are stored in —. Click the save indicator in the header to open the folder.
  • Every 5 minutes a version goes into history/ (the last 30 are kept).
  • Your session is also kept in the browser: if you close the window, everything is restored next time.
  • Export ▾ saves the final SRT or WebVTT (and the translation) wherever you choose.
help.keys:
Keyboard shortcuts

All shortcuts can be changed in ⚙ Settings → Shortcuts, and every action is in the command palette (Cmd/Ctrl K).
help.faq:
Troubleshooting

The video doesn’t play

The browser plays MP4 (H.264/AAC), WebM and most MOV files. For MKV or other formats, use the desktop app with ffmpeg installed (brew install ffmpeg): they are converted automatically.

The waveform doesn’t appear

The file may have no audio track, or it may be very large: click Waveform to generate it manually.

Transcription is very slow

It is probably running on the CPU. Use Chrome, Edge or the desktop app with GPU acceleration, or pick the tiny model.

A shortcut doesn’t work on my keyboard

Some keyboard layouts use those keys for special characters. Change it in ⚙ Settings → Shortcuts.

Where are my files?

Working copies are in the folder shown under Saving & export. Exported files go wherever you saved them.
